name: miniDSP
_refused: Read 2026-11-25 at https://www.minidsp.com/aboutus/website-terms-of-use, « Last Updated: March 16, 2026 ». THREE independently sufficient clauses. Under COPYRIGHT: « All content included on www.miniDSP.com including, without limitation, text, graphics, logos, button icons, images, audio clips, digital downloads, data compilations, DATA SHEETS, and software, is the property of miniDSP or its suppliers or partners and is protected by United States, international copyright laws, and other intellectual property laws and shall not be used for any purposes by you unless consented to, in writing, on a case-by-case basis, by miniDSP » - and note that it names DATA SHEETS among the protected content, which is precisely what this catalogue takes. Under LICENSE AND SITE ACCESS: « miniDSP grants you a limited license to access and make personal and informational use of this site [...] This license does not include: any resale or commercial use of this site or its contents; any collection and use of any product listings, descriptions, or prices; any derivative use of this site or its contents; [...] or any use of data mining, robots or similar data gathering, and extraction tools. » followed by « This site or any portion of this site may not be reproduced, duplicated, copied, sold, resold, visited or otherwise exploited for any commercial purpose without the express written consent of miniDSP. » And under PROHIBITED USES: « to scrape, crawl, harvest or otherwise collect information or data from the website, including by using automated tools such as bots, spiders or data-mining technologies, without the prior written consent of miniDSP. » No product page was opened for its specifications and no record will exist under this brand. Footer: « Copyright (c) 2009-2026 by miniDSP Ltd. », entity in Kowloon, Hong Kong, disputes under HKIAC arbitration.
_the_clause_covers_the_DOCUMENTATION_hos: Its first line settles the scope question that a reader had flagged: « All references to www.miniDSP.com shall include any subdomains and other websites operated by miniDSP. » So docs.minidsp.com, where the SHD, DDRC and nanoDIGI manuals live, and support.minidsp.com, miniDSP's Freshdesk knowledge base, are both covered - and harvesting either while the main host's clause stood unread would have been an end-run around the gate. The reader saw that and refused to do it, which was right.
_the_browser_answered_what_the_fetcher_c: Both terms pages returned 403 Forbidden to every automated client, repeatedly and spaced out, so the reader stopped at the gate and said so precisely: a terms page demonstrably exists at a known URL, which is NOT the « no terms page found » case, and an unreadable terms page is not permission. It was then read in a browser, which is the third time today that route has resolved a 403 - after dCS and Devialet - and the third time the answer turned out to be a prohibition. The 403 itself is NOT Anthropic-specific: a static path under /images/documents/ returned 404 rather than 403, so the block is generic anti-bot on HTML.
_and_its_robots_txt_names_Anthropic_expl: Measured the same day, and worth separating from the clause above because the two are different instruments. www.minidsp.com/robots.txt carries, with the maker's own comments: « # anthropic-ai is Anthropic's web crawler / User-agent: anthropic-ai / Disallow: / » and « # Claude-Web is Claude's web crawler / User-agent: Claude-Web / Disallow: / », alongside the same treatment for GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, CCBot and others. There is NO Content-Signal line, and Claude-User - the agent that reads for a person - is not named, while the « User-agent: * » group disallows only infrastructure paths. Under the decision of 2026-11-25 that reading for a person is permitted where a maker's signal allows reference, that file alone would have left the question open. The prose clause closes it, which is the right order: a robots.txt governs fetching and a contract governs reuse. Note also that docs.minidsp.com's own robots.txt names no Anthropic agent at all, and that its sitemap sits behind a Cloudflare bot-detection interstitial the reader correctly declined to pass.
_what_is_lost: The whole SHD, DDRC and nanoDIGI range, and one item in particular: miniDSP's processors impose a fixed internal sample rate on everything they touch, which is the single most consequential thing a room-correction device can tell an upsampling engine - and whether it can be turned off. Nothing was learned either way; it is recorded as absent, not guessed. This was the most valuable question on the brief and the harvest reached none of it.
_it_can_be_lifted: All three clauses are conditioned on written consent - « consented to, in writing, on a case-by-case basis », « the express written consent of miniDSP », « the prior written consent of miniDSP ». On the letter list.
